questions.q: A form of business organisation owned, financed, and managed by a single individual is called:
questions.explain: A **Sole Proprietorship** (or one-man business) is defined as a business unit owned and directed by one person who bears all the risks and takes all the profits.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major disadvantage of a sole proprietorship?
questions.explain:
**Unlimited liability** means that if the business fails and owes debts, the owner's personal properties (e.g., house, car) can be seized and sold to pay off the business debts. This is the biggest risk of a sole proprietorship.

*Other options listed (Quick decision making, Secrecy, Ease of formation) are all **advantages**.*

questions.q: The one-man business is highly popular among local traders primarily because:
options: It has a perpetual existence independent of the owner.
It requires a very large amount of capital to establish.
It is easy and cheap to set up with little legal formality.
The owner is compelled by law to share profits with employees.
questions.explain: The sole proprietorship requires minimal capital and almost **no legal formalities** (aside from perhaps local permits) to start, making it highly accessible and easy to establish for local traders.

questions.q: The legal maximum number of persons required to form an ordinary trading partnership is:
questions.explain: According to the Companies and Allied Matters Act, an ordinary partnership must consist of a minimum of **$2$** members and a maximum of **$20$** members (or up to $10$ for a banking partnership).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society

questions.q: One advantage a partnership has over a sole proprietorship is:
options: Access to more capital and combined skills
Limited liability for all regular members
questions.explain: Because a partnership consists of between $2$ to $20$ people, the partners can pool their resources together, resulting in **greater capital** and a combination of diverse managerial skills, which a single sole trader lacks.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society

questions.q: The principle that the death, insanity, or withdrawal of a major partner can lead to the end of the business indicates that partnerships often lack:
questions.explain: **Perpetual succession** is the continuation of a business regardless of the death or departure of its owners. Both sole proprietorships and ordinary partnerships lack this, whereas limited liability companies possess it.

questions.q: The formal written agreement that guides the conduct and regulates the activities of members in a partnership business is known as the:
questions.explain: The **Deed of Partnership** is the legal document drawn up to state the rules, profit-sharing ratios, capital contributions, and operational guidelines to prevent future disputes among partners.

questions.q: A business organization recognized by law as a separate legal entity, distinct from its owners, is referred to as a:
questions.explain: A **Limited Liability Company (LLC)** enjoys an independent corporate existence. This means the company can sue, be sued, and own property in its own name, completely separate from its shareholders.

questions.q: The two main classifications of Limited Liability Companies are:
questions.explain:
Limited Liability Companies are categorized into:
1. **Private Limited Companies (Ltd.)**: Cannot sell shares to the general public.
2. **Public Limited Companies (Plc.)**: Can sell shares to the general public via the stock exchange.

questions.q: What does the term "limited liability" mean for the shareholders of a company?
options: They are strictly restricted from selling their shares to the public.
They are allowed to make only a legally limited amount of profit per year.
They are liable for the company's debts only up to the exact amount of capital they contributed.
They have limited voting rights at the Annual General Meetings.
questions.explain: **Limited liability** protects the personal wealth of investors. If the company goes bankrupt, shareholders only lose the money they invested in purchasing their shares. Their personal assets (homes, bank accounts) cannot be seized to pay corporate debts.

questions.q: A major disadvantage of a Public Limited Liability Company compared to a Sole Proprietorship is:
options: Inability to raise a large amount of capital
Loss of privacy due to the required publication of annual financial accounts
High risk of personal asset seizure for business debts
questions.explain: By law, a Public Limited Company (Plc) must **publish its audited financial accounts annually** for public viewing. This strips away the financial secrecy and privacy that a sole proprietor enjoys.

questions.q: An association of individuals with common interests who pool their resources voluntarily to promote their own economic welfare is called a:
questions.explain: A **Co-operative Society** is a voluntary association formed to protect and promote the mutual economic interests and welfare of its members, rather than strictly for profit maximization.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.topic: Entrepreneurial Skill: Forms of Business Organisation

questions.q: In a Co-operative Society, surplus profit at the end of the trading period is usually distributed to members in the form of:
options: Dividends based on their level of patronage or purchases
Fixed interest rates on personal bank accounts
Equal cash gifts regardless of contribution
Promissory notes for future business investments
questions.explain: A core principle of co-operatives is that surplus (profit) is distributed back to members in proportion to their **patronage** (how much they bought from or traded with the society), not necessarily based entirely on capital contribution.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society

questions.q: Which of the following is a frequent disadvantage or problem faced by Co-operative Societies?
options: Having too much capital which leads to financial wastage
Poor management due to the reliance on unqualified members as executives
The government taking over all their trading profits
Unlimited liability for all ordinary members of the society
questions.explain: Because committee members are often elected from the ordinary membership to run the society democratically on a voluntary or low-pay basis, Co-operative Societies frequently suffer from **poor management and lack of professional administrative skills**.

questions.q: The following forms of business organizations aim primarily to maximize profit for their owners EXCEPT the:
questions.explain:
While most private sector businesses exist to maximize profit, Co-operative Societies are established with a primary mandate of service and welfare for their members.

| Form of Business | Primary Objective |
|---|---|
| Sole Proprietorship | Maximum Profit |
| Partnership | Maximum Profit |
| Public Limited Co. | Maximum Profit (for Shareholders) |
| **Co-operative Society** | **Members' Welfare & Mutual Help** |
